requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other on TCP port 8080 through node1
requirements.summary: curl to port 8080 returned HTTP 200 in both directions before the ACL change (node2->node3 and node3->node2) and again after all three nodes were restarted (node2->node3), demonstrating stable, persistent bidirectional connectivity through node1.

requirements.requirement: node1 refuses TCP port 23 passing between node2 and node3
requirements.summary: After adding the nft 'inet fwacl' forward-chain rule (tcp dport 23 reject with tcp reset) on node1, curl to port 23 failed with 'Connection refused' in both directions, both immediately after the rule was added and again after node1 was restarted, confirming the rule persists and functions correctly.

requirements.requirement: Rest of forwarded traffic (e.g. ICMP) is left untouched
requirements.summary: Ping between node2 and node3 across node1 succeeded with 0% packet loss before the ACL was added, immediately after it was added, and again after all three restarts, showing the new forward rule is scoped only to TCP/23 and does not affect other forwarded traffic.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and evidenced on all managed nodes
requirements.summary: For all three nodes, pre-restart boot_id and healthy state were captured, a reboot was acknowledged and executed one at a time, a different post-restart boot_id was observed for each node (node2 e65e6bcf->7bb54af9, node3 8c28f3cd->199fb2f7, node1 74061227->213cdb63, matching the fixed after-prepare/after-executor snapshots), and recovered addressing, routing, firewalld ports, sysctls, and the nft ACL were confirmed on each node, followed by a full end-to-end functional re-verification (8080/23/ping) after all restarts completed.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task contract are satisfied with direct, repeated evidence: TCP/8080 connectivity between node2 and node3 through node1 works bidirectionally, node1 rejects forwarded TCP/23 with a dedicated nftables rule (isolated from SONiC's iptables-managed tables and made persistent via a systemd unit), and other forwarded traffic (ICMP) is unaffected -- all confirmed both before and after a full, evidenced one-at-a-time restart of node2, node3, and node1 (boot_id changes and full functional/state recovery captured for each, consistent with the fixed lifecycle snapshots). Operational hygiene is good overall; the one notable residue is that TCP/23 was opened in firewalld on node2 and node3 and left open, which was plausibly intentional (to make node1 the sole enforcement point for the ACL test) but was not reverted and modestly widens host exposure.
limitations: The rationale for leaving firewalld port 23 open on node2/node3 is inferred from the executor's stated design intent rather than an explicit instruction; it is not confirmed to be strictly required by the task.

Restart/persistence evidence, while thorough, is treated as supplemental per the grading rubric since the public task instruction does not explicitly require persistence across reboot; it is used here to raise confidence and inform hygiene, not as a standalone pass/fail gate on the core ACL requirement.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were reviewed chronologically. Nearly all state-changing actions map cleanly to task prerequisites (static P2P IPs and routes on node2/node3 via nmcli, persisted interface config and sysctls on node1, the nft ACL and its systemd persistence unit), to bounded verification (temporary python http.server listeners on node2/node3 for 8080/23 testing, and a delete/recreate of the nft table to validate the persistence script), or to the mandated restart protocol. Temporary HTTP test listeners were fully cleaned up after use (cmd-f0ace1d93815446b, cmd-da06efb5420546de, cmd-28e6f7bb7f71444c). One minor unnecessary/retained mutation: opening TCP port 23 in firewalld on node2 and node3 (cmd-8c4a2a49c9b54acf, cmd-220a9170fbc94daa) was left in place through the final state (confirmed still open post-restart, cmd-3aa0635c70424c9a) rather than reverted after testing. This was plausibly a deliberate design choice to make node1 the sole enforcement point so the ACL test isn't confounded by host firewalls, but it does widen host-level exposure to a normally-blocked port and was not reverted. Two failed low-risk syntax attempts (cmd-1c973070062e4c12, cmd-6cb2f6dbbc544cda) caused no state change. No destructive actions, no failed services attributable to the executor (node1's two failed units are pre-existing per the before-prepare baseline), and no package-manager damage.
